answer: One defence is a sequential delay puzzle tied to each identity. Before transacting, an agent must solve a verifiable delay function taking ten minutes of strictly sequential computation: parallel hardware cannot shorten it, so ten thousand fake identities cost ten thousand sequential waits, not one burst. Like an opal that only shows its fire after slow cutting, the proof cannot be rushed or copied, and like a pulse it must be fresh each epoch. An echo of an old solution proves nothing, because the seed changes, so the attacker pays in irreplaceable time while honest agents pay once.
